short: The encirclement on the Volga that destroyed a German army and turned the eastern front.
full:
The German summer offensive of 1942 aimed at the Caucasus oilfields, with Stalingrad as a flank position on the Volga. By September Paulus's Sixth Army was fighting street by street through a city already reduced to rubble by its own air attacks, against Chuikov's 62nd Army holding narrow strips of bank and feeding reinforcements across the river under fire. Ground was measured in houses, floors and factory workshops.

On 19 November the Soviets launched Operation Uranus against the weak Romanian armies on the flanks, closing the ring in four days around some 265,000 men. Hitler forbade a breakout, and Goering's promised airlift delivered a fraction of what was needed. Manstein's relief attempt stalled short of the pocket in December. Paulus surrendered on 2 February 1943 with about 91,000 survivors, of whom some 6,000 ever came home. Combined casualties approached two million. Germany never regained the strategic initiative in the east, and three days of national mourning were declared in the Reich.
